channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] After the poison of Saxony-Anhalt, Berlin election could be the antidote
item.description: We hear a lot about extremism in Germany, after the breakthrough of the AfD earlier this month. Yet a far-left government may be about to take power in Berlin on Sunday, and is attracting almost no attention. Why is that?

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s ‘European values,’ paid for by private equity, powered by Claude
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen talks about European sovereignty and keeping Europe’s fate in European hands, but the model she presented for achieving that sovereignty relies heavily on non-European technology and global capital.

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] Belgian minister under fire for denying evacuation to 13 Gazan scholarship students
item.description: Belgium's minister for migration was accused of being "the shame of this government" during a heated debate on Wednesday on the fate of 13 Gazans who won scholarships to Belgian universities but have been denied transport so that they can take up their places.

item.title: [EU Observer] Turkey’s anti-LGBTI+ crackdown draws meek EU criticism
item.description: Turkey has arrested dozens of LGBTI+ activists in nationwide raids, drawing meek criticism from EU officials and calls for Europe-wide solidarity protests on Friday.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [EU Observer] We lied to ourselves again, Russians write, as Ukrainians reportedly advance beyond the Zherebets river (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,665)
item.description: Ukrainians brace for another winter of blackouts, but are still overwhelmingly continuing resistance.

item.title: [EU Observer] Former Kosovo leader is war criminal rules EU-backed court, tearing open old Western Balkans wounds
item.description: Hashim Thaçi was convicted for "torture against 303 individuals and murder against 96 individuals", prompting angry protests by Kosovo nationalists in The Hague and Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] Did Europe’s ‘summer of truth’ push climate up von der Leyen’s agenda? Yes, but there were some shocking omissions
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the devastating impacts of climate change during her State of the Union address, including hectares of land burned, crops lost and additional heatwave-related deaths.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen set to cave in to Greek asylum-busting demands
item.description: The Greeks suspended asylum in 2020. They did it again last year. The EU commission endorsed both. Greece last month asked for new EU rules to suspend asylum and the commission appears to have complied.

item.title: [EU Observer] Canada’s Carney gets the red carpet treatment and EU ‘associate member’ offer
item.description: EU commission president Ursula von der Leyen offered unprecedented 'associate member' status of the bloc to Canada on Wednesday. But what could this mean in practice?

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin and Netanyhau will be laughing at EU after von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech
item.description: EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen's answer to spiralling Russian aggression was one new strategy document and two new sets of meetings. Her answer to Israel's killing spree was to call it "unacceptable".

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Russia has never stopped thinking like an empire — here’s how it shapes and may break the Kremlin
item.description: When other empires stopped expanding, Russia refused to stop. "Perhaps Russia was too successful for too long," argues political geographer Michael Romancov. He explained that over five centuries of land grabs worked for so long it became part of Russia's "genetic make-up".

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What should Europeans expect from Ursula von der Leyen on climate?
item.description: With summer droughts, fires and rising food insecurity fresh in mind, von der Leyen is expected to weigh only modest moves like a new Water Act and climate-risk plan.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [EU Observer] The EU’s 15 year self-declared war against migrant smugglers is a deadly joke
item.description: Magnus Brunner, the EU migration commissioner, makes an impassioned plea to tackle migrant smugglers. The EU has been saying the same thing for the past 15 years, yet profits remain high and people continue to die.

item.title: [DW] Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
item.description: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s State of the Union likely to tiptoe around China ahead of trade showdown
item.description: The EU's competitiveness problems and its trade dispute with China have not gone away, but Ursula von der Leyen won't pile on the criticism of Beijing at Wednesday's State of the Union address, as trade talks enter the crunch stage.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU sanctions needed against Russian bot and troll factories, MEPs say
item.description: The parliament supports the European Democracy Shield proposal and calls for sanctions to fight Russian disinformation campaigns.

item.title: [DW] Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
item.description: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

item.title: [DW] Europe launches two climate observation satellites
item.description: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI discloses new ‘concerning’ model behaviour
item.description: Developer launches system to track and report AI model misconduct

item.title: [Politico Europe] What does a party of former PMs reveal?
item.description: What happens when the keys to Number 10 are handed back? Anne reports from a gathering of former prime ministers – Rishi Sunak and Keir Starmer – and reveals what life after power really looks like. Meanwhile, after some football diplomacy with Canadian PM Mark Carney, could it offer a chance for Andy Burnham to […]

item.description: US president threatens to impose ‘very serious’ tariffs on the bloc if the measure is approved

item.description: A clearer reaction function is a fine substitute for forward guidance

item.title: [Financial Times] HSBC axes $38,000 school fee perk for new Hong Kong bankers
item.description: Longstanding subsidy had been used to attract senior staff to Asian financial hub

item.title: [Politico Europe] King Charles: Pace of AI is ‘deeply concerning’
item.description: The British monarch will tell tech CEOS the world wants "reassurance that we will not lose control of our destiny.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Von der Leyen makes it awkward with Canada
item.description: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney takes the stage in Strasbourg after Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised EU capitals by floating “associate membership” for Canada — a status that doesn’t actually exist, and that Ottawa itself seems reluctant to define. Zoya Sheftalovich and Sarah Wheaton ask whether von der Leyen got ahead of both […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump fails to bend the Fed to his will
item.description: Kevin Warsh leads the US central bank to its first rate rise since 2023 less than four months into the job

item.title: [Financial Times] Apple’s most valuable product isn’t the iPhone
item.description: Markets were signalling discomfort even before the latest wave of worries about existential risk

item.title: [Financial Times] EU asks China to voluntarily limit hybrid car exports
item.description: Move comes as cheaper Chinese vehicles flood European market

item.title: [Financial Times] Where do new jobs come from?
item.description: The centuries-old trend towards specialisation could be about to reverse

item.title: [Financial Times] Thousands of Barclays staff revolt against three-day office mandate
item.description: Push for bank to grant exemptions for employees with longer commutes and one-off payments to cover rise in workers’ costs

item.title: [Financial Times] DeepMind offshoot nears $4bn valuation just a month after founding
item.description: Researchers leaving Big Tech group’s London lab close to raising $700mn for new start-up Emulate

item.title: [Financial Times] The era of AI warfare has arrived
item.description: Autonomous systems are being rapidly integrated on the battlefield, as models advance in ways even their creators cannot fully predict

item.title: [Politico Europe] Kann die Tanksäule den Kanzler aus Krise retten?
item.description: Rekordpreise an den Zapfsäulen und der Kanzler versucht sein Standing zu retten, auch indem er Entlastung verspricht. Doch die Koalition streitet über das richtige Rezept zur Entlastung.Während SPD-Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil auf eine saubere Gegenfinanzierung pocht, will Friedrich Merz direkte Auszahlungen an die Bevölkerung. Für ihn steht nach bitteren Wahlniederlagen in Sachsen-Anhalt viel auf dem Spiel: […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] In Ceuta, it’s up to Europe to clean up the Spanish government’s mess
item.description: Europe must reckon with the failure of the leadership in Madrid and do everything to prevent a worsening of the crisis.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage aide caught in donor sting attended Egypt retreat with JL Partners
item.description: The polling company invited a top Nigel Farage lieutenant as a guest speaker.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Don’t get ‘locked in’ by EU rules, top nuclear adviser warns Burnham
item.description: John Fingleton tells POLITICO "risk aversion" in Whitehall must not slow Britain's dash for new nuclear.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Friedrich Merz’s endgame: All the scenarios, rated
item.description: Germany's chancellor is on the brink. We map out what happens next.

item.title: [Politico Europe] In Germany’s east, a rare center-left star looks to stem the far right’s rise
item.description: State premier Manuela Schwesig is close to stopping the AfD’s advance ahead of Sunday’s regional elections — but at a great cost to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europa tiene que solucionar ahora el desastre provocado por el Gobierno español en Ceuta
item.description: Europa debe afrontar el fracaso del liderazgo en Madrid y hacer todo lo posible para evitar que la crisis empeore.

item.title: [DW] Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

item.title: [DW] EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
item.description: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
item.description: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

item.title: [DW] Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
item.description: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.
